members.name: Sione
members.thread: A freelance web developer in the study: sites, code and invoices.

character.lede: A lakeside cottage gathers blue-green board-and-batten cross-gables under olive shingle, with a flat meadow-roofed glass sunroom. A dense cottage garden runs down to a creek with a jetty and a rowboat.

spots.line: An easel, a bistro table and hanging ferns fill the glass sunroom.
A fireplace, a task chair and a desk lamp make the study.
Café curtains and a bread bin brighten the kitchen.

facts.style: Single-storey lakeside cottage: a cluster of blue-green board-and-batten cross-gables under olive shingle, a raised entry landing two steps over a sunken open living room, a flat meadow-roofed glass sunroom, a creek with a jetty and rowboat in a dense cottage garden

character.truths: The Core sits on a writing desk in the Study. A television and a fireplace are in the Living Room and the Study. No kitchen island. The garage has a washer, a dryer, a workbench and a bicycle. Creek, jetty and rowboat beyond the garden.

inkscape: Runs as a remote-desktop style session in the browser, not a native window
Image tag is the Kasm image version, not the Inkscape version
wordpress: [public-access] A public site needs your Core reachable from outside. Open it by its public URL, not the .localhost link.
A site nobody outside can open is not a site
open-webui: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Open WebUI as a featured app.
[cloud-link] It can also connect to cloud models with an API key. Leave that off.
[note] Wired to the Core's local model by the Hub (hub_integration inference). Say "a model on the Core"; never claim it matches a hosted model and never give a speed figure.
Can connect to cloud models with an API key (field in the install form): leave out of any scene.
Hub wires it to the local model.
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
glasshome: Listing and notes say entity data never leaves the network: do not repeat the absolute.
Optional community widgets come from an outside hub.
joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
jellyfin: [note] Plays your own files. Say that, not "Netflix".
[claims] Do not say it plays copyrighted material from anywhere.
Plays your own media only: never "streams any movie".
QA capture is the setup wizard with a container id as the server name; the gallery frame is a demo library with lurid exploitation film posters: neither usable.
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
n8n: [licence] Fair-code licence, not open source. Say "source-available"; do not say "open source".
[note] An n8n MCP entry exists for agents.
Fair-code licence: say source-available, never open source.
Public URL setting is for webhooks; leave off the scene.
Listing says full control over data: connectors to cloud services still pass data to them.
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
listmonk: [cloud-link] Sending at volume needs an SMTP provider or mail server. Do not promise delivery.
penpot: Five containers (frontend, backend, exporter, Postgres, Redis).
QA screenshot is the log-in page: reject.
Listing images show community library tiles: marketing.
code-server: [cloud-link] The editor and the files are on the Core and it asks for no cloud key. Installing an extension fetches it from an outside extension registry (the upstream default is Open VSX), and a coding agent extension c

[claims] The listing says "access it from anywhere"; do not write that (the sheet leaves remote access unfinished). Say the editor opens in the laptop's browser on the home network. Never claim it matches a hosted coding
[note] One password set at install (plus an optional sudo password). It is one household tool, not a separate account per person.
[note] Persona decision 2026-10-15 (Liam Broza): re-admitted from the old cloud-or-developer exclusion for the builder archetype. The manifest has no API key field.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core
Heavy for a client tool: three containers
invoice-ninja: [cloud-link] Taking card payments needs a payment provider. Say invoicing, not payment processing.
privatebin: Footer of the screen says the server has "zero knowledge": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and Enclosed: one per household
readeck: listing says securely: do not repeat
QA shot is the first-run form
teampass: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Listing claims secrets never leave the appliance (banned word, banned claim)
Per-person roles sit close to the cap-multi-user rule: phrase it as the app's folders and permissions
endurain: [cloud-link] Optional sync with Strava and Garmin Connect. Bulk GPX and FIT upload is local.
Strava and Garmin sync are outside links: say bulk upload is the local path
GPS history is location data: story must not map a home address
bentopdf: Dual licence: AGPL-3.0 or paid commercial; fine for household use
Listing says "nothing to leak": drop that wording
radicale: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
no QA screenshot (the app has a bare web page)
